High Court Of Madhya Pra
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Shri Aviral Vikas Khare, learned couns  Shri Hemant Sharma G.A., learned Gover  respondent/State.
Heard on the question of admission.
Admit.
Let the record of the Courts below be requisitioned.
Heard on I.A.No.6401/2022, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant.

The applicant has been convicted for offence under Sections 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo 6 months R.I. with fine of Rs.6,000/- with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime.
He further submits that the sample was taken from the lot which was not kept for sale in the shop, rather it was kept by the applicant in his house for disposal.
The entire prosecution case is based on the testimony of B.S.Solanki (PW-1), the Food Inspector.
Nothing is stated regarding the mandatory compliance of provisions of Section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

As per the statement of Dilip Kumar (PW-3), notice under Section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act was sent to the applicant on 16.02.2009, but acknowledgment Ex.P-25 is dated 14.02.2009, so SAN REENA JOSEPH Date: 2022.05.10 it is not possible that the notice dated 16.02.2009 was received by the applicant, 18:04:38 IST as the acknowledgment receipt depicts the date as 14.02.2009.

It is also submitted that (DW-1), the applicant categorically stated in his statement that packets were kept in the Almirah of the house and the Food Inspector searched the house and there is no denial of this statement.
It is also submitted that the applicant is aged about 82 years.
There is no possibility of early hearing of this revision.

Under these circumstances, counsel Shri Govind Das Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54140383/
1 prays for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail to the applicant.

entities.text: Govind Das Gupta vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State o n t h e other hand, has opposed the bail application by submitting that no sufficient ground is made out for releasing the applicant on bail,
hence the application filed by the applicant be dismissed.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, the quantum of sentence imposed upon the applicant, this Court is of the considered opinion that the application for suspension of jail sentence filed on behalf of the applicant deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly, I.A.No.6401/2022 is allowed and it is directed that on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, the execution of jail sentence of the applicant shall remain suspended,
till the final disposal of this revision for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 29.08.2022 and thereafter on all such subsequent dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this regard.
List for final hearing in due course.
I.A.No.6401/2022 is disposed off.
SAN REENA JOSEPH
Date: 2022.05.10  18:04:38 IST  C.C. as per rules.
(RAJENDRA KUMAR (VERMA))
JUDGE  RJ
